body: Hansen's (1935 juice co.) went bankrupt 1988; Rodney Sacks and Hilton Schlosberg bought it and listed it 1990 at pennies. 1990s energy drinks went nowhere; the Monster brand launched 2002 and the company took off. CNBC: ~+200,000% from Feb 1994 to Feb 2024 ($1k -> ~$2m; $55.02 close Feb 2024); ~42% CAGR over the 20 years to 2023 (BusinessTech). Splits 2:1 2005, 4:1 2006, 2:1 2012, 3:1 2016, 2:1 2023 (96x cumulative): a ~$5 2003 Hansen share is ~$0.05 today [split math mine; 2003 price unverified]. Max drawdown: roughly -70% in 2007-08 [unverified]. Growth was overwhelmingly sales/EPS (31 consecutive years of sales growth); P/E rose from low-teens to 30-40x [unverified]. EARLY SIGNAL visible 2003-05: a tiny company with a new brand growing sales >50%/yr, ~50% gross margins, fully outsourced production (co-packers) and distribution through beer distributors (capital-light), plus action-sports marketing creating a youth category. Coca-Cola's 16.7% stake for >$2bn (2014) and 2015 distribution swap were late confirmation, not the signal. Who caught it: the insiders (Sacks/Schlosberg, large owners); no well-documented famous early outside investor found. Stall: growth slowed to low-teens by 2023-24; stock range-bound ~2021-24. LESSON: a boring-looking small consumer company that creates a category, outsources the capital, and keeps the same owner-managers can compound for decades; the obvious-in-hindsight signal was unit growth + gross margin + zero capex, not a famous holder.

data.early_signals: new brand >50% sales growth, ~50% GM, outsourced bottling + beer-distributor network

title: Monster Beverage (Hansen Natural): best US stock of 30 years
